=== New report: Mean Time Between Failure

- Available under *Reports* in Portal to Org Admins only, in the *Device* category.
- Measures the average time, in hours, that devices remain online and available between offline events. Higher MTBF values indicate greater device stability and reliability.
- Charts MTBF trends over time, summarized by week, for a date range you select.
- A week with no offline events shows an MTBF of 1000 hours. This value is a placeholder, not a measurement.

=== Scriptless Automation

Scriptless test runs now end sooner when a device can't start the test, and they report the actual error instead of "Device retry exceeded". Previously, these runs could retry for about an hour and a half before failing with that general message.

* Fixed an issue where a run whose app is not on the target device, with no App Repository version to install, retried repeatedly. The run now ends after the first attempt with an *Init session failed* status and the device's error message.
* Fixed an issue where a test case recorded only on the device home screen launched the home screen. The run now ends after the first attempt.
* Fixed an issue where a test case that included a system screen without an app identifier, such as Camera on iOS, failed to start. The run now continues with the other apps in the test case.
* Runs that keep failing to start now end with the last error the device reported instead of "Device retry exceeded".

// Source: KOB-55190 from PR #820
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/820

=== Parallel Sessions report includes retained devices

- The *Parallel Sessions* report now counts retained devices toward peak parallel sessions, even when no session is running on the retained device.
- A device that is retained and in an active session at the same time is counted once.
- Report data from July 2026 onward reflects the updated count.

== Kobiton CLI

- Fixed `kobiton file push` and `kobiton file pull` reporting success and exiting `0` when the transfer failed on the device. A push to a path the device refuses, a push to an iOS app that is not installed, and a pull of a file that does not exist now exit with a non-zero status. This applies to iOS devices, iOS simulators, and Android devices.
- Fixed `kobiton file push` to iOS devices and iOS simulators intermittently failing with an error even though the file was written.

=== Turbo Test Execution

* *Session reliability:* Fixed an issue where running Turbo Test sessions could end unexpectedly when a scheduled background authentication renewal failed. The renewal now retries automatically, so running Turbo Test sessions continue while the authentication service is briefly unavailable.

// Source: KOB-55531 from PR #799
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/799

== Fixed devices stuck after Appium 2 scripts in mixed sessions

Fixed an issue in mixed sessions on Android devices where the device remained on the *Lightning Mode is turning off* screen after a basic Appium 2 script finished. The next script on the same device could not view or interact with the device until the session was exited and reopened.

Consecutive Appium 2 scripts now run on the same device in a mixed session without exiting the session. Manual interaction with the device is also available after a script ends.

// Source: KOB-55556 from PR #795
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/795

== Session data archiving

* Kobiton now archives sessions with hundreds of megabytes of recorded command data in smaller parts. Previously, archiving these sessions ran out of memory and restarted repeatedly, which stopped all session archiving.
* When Kobiton can't archive a session, it skips that session and continues archiving the remaining sessions.

// Source: KOB-55541 from PR #792
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/792

== Kobiton CLI

- Fixed an issue where a failed `kobiton file push` or `kobiton file pull` did not show the reason reported by the device. The CLI now displays the device's reason, such as `Error sending file: couldn't create file: Read-only file system.`, and exits with a non-zero code. Successful transfers are not affected.

// Source: KOB-55547 from PR #791
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/791

== Kobiton CLI

- Fixed an issue where `kobiton file pull` stopped partway through a large file transfer from an Android device without reporting an error or exiting. Large pulls now complete, and the pulled file matches the file on the device.

// Source: KOB-55514 from PR #790
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/790

== Inspector and page source now load for iOS screens with unbounded elements

Fixed an issue on iOS devices where *Inspector* displayed no XML hierarchy, and Appium page source requests failed with a `JSON serialization failed` error, when the screen contained an element that iOS reports with an unbounded position or size.

Kobiton now returns these elements with a position of `-1, -1` and a width and height of `0`, matching Appium behavior, so the rest of the page loads. All other elements are returned unchanged.

The fix applies to the iOS *Inspector* XML hierarchy, page source, and find element results.

// Source: KOB-55562 from PR #786
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/786

== Turbo Test Execution

- Fixed an issue where Turbo Test sessions could stop starting, and later time out, after test executors lost and restored their connections at the same time, for example after a brief network interruption or an executor restart.
- New Turbo Test sessions now go only to test executors that are online. Executors that stop responding are removed within about 15 seconds.
- A Turbo Test session whose executor connection drops now fails quickly with the status message `Executor connection lost`, instead of waiting up to 15 minutes to time out.

// Source: KOB-55522 from PR #774
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/774

== Get Element Attribute returns null for missing attributes on iOS

On iOS native automation sessions, the WebDriver Get Element Attribute command now returns `null` when an element does not have the requested attribute. Android sessions already behave this way.

Previously, these requests returned an HTTP 500 error. Appium clients retried the failed request several times, so the error could take about 25 seconds to appear.

Requests for attributes that an element has, such as `type` and `enabled`, still return their values.

// Source: KOB-55525 from PR #772
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/772

=== Usage report

* Updated the xref:reporting:usage-report/use-the-report.adoc[usage report] to record session data, including session counts, minutes, and validation counts, when a session ends instead of on a periodic schedule.
* Validation results that finish after a session ends now update that session's counts in the usage report.

The report contents and how you view the report are unchanged.

== Run deviceConnect on Linux hosts for Android devices

deviceConnect can now run on a Linux host to connect Android devices to Kobiton. Previously, deviceConnect required a Mac mini host.

* deviceConnect is available as a `.deb` package for Debian-based distributions and an `.rpm` package for Red Hat-based distributions.
* The package bundles the runtime and Android tools that deviceConnect uses, and installs deviceConnect as system services.
* Configuration changes you make on the host are kept when you upgrade deviceConnect.
* Uninstall deviceConnect with your distribution's package manager.

Linux hosts support Android devices only. iOS devices continue to require a Mac mini host. deviceConnect and GigaCap cannot be installed on the same Linux host.

For hardware requirements, see xref:device-lab-management:deviceConnect/hardware-requirements-for-deviceconnect.adoc[].

== Android web automation sessions

- Fixed an issue where an Appium session in Chrome or in an app WebView on an Android device stopped responding when a click opened a JavaScript dialog, such as an alert or confirm dialog. The dialog appeared on the device, but the click command did not return, and later commands, including the command to end the session, also did not return. The session stayed active and the device stayed in use until the session was terminated from Kobiton Portal or the Kobiton API. The fix also applies to double taps and to typing commands that tap the element first. Clicks that do not open a dialog work as before.

== Kobiton MCP server: optional `userIntent`

AI assistants connected to the Kobiton MCP server no longer have to send `userIntent` with every tool call, and the tool definitions they load are smaller.

- A tool call without `userIntent` now runs instead of failing. When a call includes `userIntent`, Kobiton still records it in the audit log exactly as sent.
- Every tool describes `userIntent` with the same one-line description, "A brief summary of why this call is being made." This reduces the tool definitions an AI assistant loads by about 1,100 tokens per session.
- `automate` plugin version 1.16.0 asks AI assistants to send `userIntent` only when the tool name and arguments don't show why a call is made, such as ending a session or deleting a test case.

For details, see xref:ai:mcp/ai-plugin-mcp-ref.adoc#_call_purpose_userintent[Call purpose (`userIntent`)].

* Instrumentation now stops and displays an error message that names the app's file format when an app uses method handles. Kobiton cannot instrument these apps.

== Cambrionix hub detection on Linux deviceConnect hosts

deviceConnect on Linux hosts now detects a Cambrionix hub connected directly to the host. Previously, the deviceConnect console showed "No USB hubs attached," and hub-based features were unavailable for devices on the host.

With the hub detected:

* *System* > *Device Gateways* in the deviceConnect console lists the hub with its serial number, its ports, and the device on each port.
* The *Slot* column in xref:device-lab-management:device-management-page.adoc[Device Management] and the *Slot* field in the *More info* panel of a manual session show the hub port of each device.
* Port modes (*Data*, *Charge*, and *Off*) are available for devices on the hub.
* The *Battery Drain* group appears on the *Metrics* tab of manual sessions.

Devices connected through the hub's USB 3.0 path do not yet show a slot.

macOS hosts and hubs connected through a Gem are not affected by this change.

This affected restarts from *Restart* in Kobiton Portal and from the Kobiton CLI `device restart` command. The simulator stayed unavailable until someone started it again on the host machine. A restarted iOS simulator now comes back *Online* with the same UDID.

- On iOS simulators, the Appium commands `mobile: queryAppState` and `mobile: isAppInstalled` now return the app state and installation status. == deviceConnect for Linux installation fixes

- Fixed an issue where deviceConnect Console was not reachable from other machines after installing the `.rpm` package on Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 hosts with firewalld enabled.
- Fixed an issue where deviceConnect Console stopped responding after a Red Hat Enterprise Linux host restarted. deviceConnect Console now remains available after a host restart.
- On Linux hosts with an active firewall, installing deviceConnect now opens TCP ports 80, 443, 10160, 10161, 10165, and 10180. On firewalld hosts, the ports open in each active zone. On Ubuntu hosts with ufw enabled, the package now adds these rules where earlier versions added none.
- On hosts with no active firewall, installing deviceConnect does not change firewall settings.
- Removing the deviceConnect package closes only the ports that the package opened. Firewall rules that an administrator added before installation remain in place.

// Source: KOB-55539 from PR #804
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/804

== Session reliability

- Fixed an issue where one unresponsive session could block other sessions on the same host. Previously, new sessions could not start, automation sessions failed, and active sessions could not end until the host was restarted.
- Appium commands and other requests sent to a session that cannot keep up now fail right away with an HTTP `503` response instead of hanging. Retry the request later.

// Source: KOB-55565 from PR #802
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/802

== Appium AI settings require Private device slots

Appium AI organization settings are now available only to organizations whose subscription includes Private device slots.

* Organizations without Private device slots no longer see the *AI Settings* tab in Kobiton Portal settings. Opening the page by its URL shows *Appium AI is not available* with a link to contact your account manager.
* Requests to read, save, or delete Appium AI settings through the API are refused for those organizations.
* Settings saved earlier are kept and return automatically when the organization adds Private device slots.
* Kobiton Standalone isn't affected.

For details, see xref:automation-testing:appium-ai/configure-appium-ai-org-settings.adoc#no-private-device-slots[Configure Appium AI settings for your organization].

// Source: KOB-55546 from PR #796
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/796

== Session Explorer: CLI sessions with many screenshots now load

Session Overview and Session Explorer now load CLI sessions that include many full-resolution screenshots. Previously, a CLI session with five or more WebDriver screenshot requests could fail to load its steps.

* *Step labels:* Session Explorer labels each WebDriver step in a CLI session with its request path, such as `GET /screenshot`.
* *Private mode:* Screenshots and page sources stay hidden in private mode for automation and CLI sessions.

// Source: KOB-55560 from PR #785
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/785

== Kobiton API

- Fixed the session commands endpoints returning more commands than Session Explorer shows for Kobiton CLI sessions. `GET /v1/sessions/\{id}/commands`, the v2 session commands endpoint, and `GET /v1/sessions/\{id}/commandsCount` now return one session creation plus one command per `kobiton webdriver` call, matching the steps in Session Explorer. Previously, these endpoints also returned the repeated `POST /wd/hub/session` request that Kobiton CLI sends before each call. This change applies to CLI sessions recorded after this release. Sessions recorded earlier are unchanged.

// Source: KOB-55544 from PR #793
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/793

== Install `.app` builds on real iOS devices in manual sessions

In manual sessions, the *Install Apps* modal now accepts `.app` builds on real iOS devices and stops installs of iOS builds that can't run on the device in use.

* *Upload File* and *Install From URL* accept a zipped `.app` on real iPhones and iPads. A device build `.app` installs the same way as an `.ipa`.
* A Simulator build on a real iOS device is rejected with a clear message before install, instead of failing during install.
* A device build on an iOS Simulator is rejected with a clear message before install.
* Android sessions and iOS builds that match the device work as before.

For details, see xref:manual-testing:install-an-app.adoc#_install_ios_app_builds[Install `.app` builds on iOS].

// Source: KOB-55056 from PR #787
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/787

=== Storage

* Standalone now automatically deletes temporary session data files that deviceConnect uploads to Kobiton storage for processing. Standalone removes any file left over after processing 24 to 48 hours after upload, so these files no longer accumulate in storage.

// Source: KOB-55554 from PR #781
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/781

== Reset device state through the Kobiton API

Organization admins can now reset the state of devices in their organization using the new `RESET_DEVICE_STATE` task of the `POST /v2/execute-admin-tasks` API.

Resetting a device sets its state to `UNPLUGGED`, clears its booked status, and takes the device offline. The reset does not send any command to the physical device or its host machine. Sessions, reservations, history, and device settings are not changed.

* Reset up to 100 online devices in one request by listing their UDIDs.
* Review the result for each device in the response. The request returns HTTP 200 even when some devices fail to reset.
* The device stays offline until deviceConnect services are restarted. For details, see xref:device-lab-management:deviceConnect/restart-deviceconnect-services.adoc[].
* If the device has a live session, the session is disconnected and ends automatically.
* A reset does not send a `deviceStateChanged` webhook or a real-time update.

Available to users with the *ADMIN* predefined role, for devices in their own organization.

For request parameters, response fields, and error codes, see the https://api.kobiton.com/docs/#kobiton-api-v2[Kobiton API v2 reference].

== Turbo Test reports

- Completed Appium Turbo Test sessions now consistently show the *Test Report* section in Session Overview, and the session details in the Kobiton API include the test report download URL. Previously, a small number of completed sessions showed no test report, even though the report was generated.

For details on downloading test reports, see xref:automation-testing:turbo-test-execution/run-appium-test.adoc#_download_test_report[Download test report].

== Crash logs in sessions

Fixed an issue where app crashes during Android and iOS sessions were not captured. Sessions now show the crash and its crash log in Session Explorer.

This fix applies to manual, Appium, and API sessions. For details, see xref:session-explorer:analytics/review-crash-logs.adoc[].
